answer: Each agent claims one tidal flat plot on a tundra shore below a summit datum post, posts a 70-credit bond, and reports its exposed area at low tide. An auditor recomputes it from the tide table and summit datum, allowing 5% error; reuse or a copied tide timestamp burns the bond and voids the identity. The first claim costs 34, the kth 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6028 and 1000 fakes cost 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked, since each plot-tide-datum triple is unique. A rented-flat ring fails since one rented plot yields one area per tide; honest agents pay 34 once and reclaim the bond after audit.
